name: Erdoğanism
summary: Erdoğanism is the political programme and style of Recep Tayyip Erdoğan and the AK Party: socially conservative, nationalist and Islam-inflected, built on a populist claim to embody the national will against secular and foreign elites. It favours a strong, centralised, personalised presidency over checks and balances, a pro-growth state-steered economy, a pious-family agenda, and an assertive Ottoman-influenced foreign policy.
scope: The mainstream of Erdoğan's rule as party leader, prime minister and president (2003 to the present), weighted toward the post-2013 'New Turkey' and 2017 presidential-system period. The early 'conservative democrat' reform phase (EU accession, liberal economy) is noted but not the baseline. Based on the Wikipedia overview, the AKP, Yilmaz and Morieson's analysis of civilizational populism, and Erdoğan's own speeches.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The AKP's health-transformation programme expanded state-funded coverage to nearly all residents, which it counts as a signature achievement.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Erdogan-era governments raise the minimum wage by decree, often before elections, but adherents frame this as a state favour rather than a principle.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The AKP began with liberal market reforms and privatisation, yet Erdogan later overrode market logic on interest rates and favoured state-guided growth.

public-ownership.rationale: The AKP carried out most of Turkey's privatisations and prefers private firms and state-backed construction contractors to public monopolies.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The party courts business and a conservative provincial middle class and has not campaigned for sharply higher taxes on the wealthy.

unions-good.rationale: Governments under Erdogan have kept union power limited and restricted strikes by decree; unions are tolerated, not championed as a social good.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property and private enterprise are protected by the AKP's market-friendly record, though eminent domain for mega-projects shows property can be overridden.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Erdogan favours state steering of business through credit and contracts but not general tighter regulation, and the party is closely tied to favoured firms.

cut-welfare.rationale: The AKP built its base partly on expanded social assistance, housing and health programmes, so it rejects welfare cuts as a goal.

worker-ownership.rationale: Collective worker ownership has no place in a conservative-nationalist, pro-business movement.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Post-2016 security politics treat terrorism as a national emergency and justify broad surveillance and anti-terror laws.

legalize-drugs.rationale: A socially conservative movement that frames the family as sacred opposes legal recreational drugs.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Turkish law restricts insulting religious values and the president, but adherents mean protecting Islam and the leader, not minorities, so the question splits.

strong-leader.rationale: Erdogan-ism is centred on a strong, charismatic leader and a presidential system with limited checks, as the Wikipedia article describes.

state-harmful.rationale: Erdogan-ism wants a strong, commanding state and nationalist statecraft; anarchist anti-statism is the opposite.

limit-guns.rationale: Turkey already regulates guns tightly and the state monopoly on force is not contested by the movement, though it has not campaigned on the issue.

empower-police-military.rationale: The movement stresses security, defence industry growth and counter-terror powers for the state after 2015-2016.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Moral conservatism and the sacred-family framing oppose legalising sex work.

decide-locally.rationale: The AKP favours strong central leadership and reduced elected local offices, as it did in 2013.

rehabilitation.rationale: Harsh treatment of terror and coup suspects suggests punishment-first, though adherents do not systematically reject rehabilitation.

traditional-family.rationale: Erdogan calls the family a sacred structure and the steel core of society, and urges at least three children.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The AKP opposes same-sex marriage and Erdogan treats LGBT rights as a threat to the family.

abortion-legal.rationale: The AKP tightened abortion practice and Erdogan has described abortion as murder, though it remains legal in early pregnancy.

more-religion-public.rationale: The project aims to move past strict secularism and raise a pious generation through schools, mosques and Diyanet.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Turkish politics does not frame racial injustice this way; the nearest analogue is redress for religious-conservative grievances against Kemalists.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Erdogan attacks what he calls desexualization policies and presents gender roles as natural and family-based.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: National-conservative revival of Ottoman-Islamic tradition is a core theme of the ideology.

gradual-change.rationale: Erdogan-ism pursues a "New Turkey" that breaks with Kemalist institutions, but it works through elections and incremental legal change rather than revolution.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The government has hosted millions of Syrian refugees and framed it as religious duty, though domestic pressure to restrict has grown.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Erdogan criticises the UN structure ("the world is bigger than five") and distrusts Western-led institutions.

free-trade.rationale: Turkey has pursued export growth and customs union ties while using tariffs and state steering when convenient.

nation-first.rationale: The AKP's rhetoric increasingly puts Turkish and Islamic-world interests above Western-led cooperation, though Turkey remains in NATO.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Turkey justified Syrian and other interventions partly on humanitarian and Muslim-solidarity grounds, yet rejects Western interventions elsewhere.

open-borders.rationale: Neither nationalism nor conservatism supports abolishing borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Erdoğan sets double-digit growth and mega-projects as national goals (s5); the source does not mention the environment.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Turkey ratified the Paris agreement late and prioritises growth and energy supply, though recent net-zero pledges exist.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Defence-industry and technology self-reliance are national pride themes, though not a doctrine of technological salvation.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The government is building Turkey's first nuclear plant at Akkuyu and plans more.

revolution-justified.rationale: Erdogan-ism claims democratic legitimacy via elections and condemns the 2016 coup attempt, treating coups and revolutions as illegitimate.

experts-over-public.rationale: Its populism claims to speak for the national will against technocratic and Kemalist elites.

central-planning.rationale: The movement is pro-business and capitalist, with state steering of investment rather than central planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: Market socialism has no standing in the movement.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not a theme; a land tax replacing others clashes with a construction-driven growth model.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not a theme, and inherited family wealth and property fit the conservative family emphasis.

basic-income.rationale: The AKP favours targeted social assistance and conditional aid rather than unconditional income.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Governments use tariffs and local-content rules for strategic sectors despite the customs union.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Erdogan directs credit and public contracts toward mega-projects, construction and the defence industry.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The party courts small provincial businesses but also depends on large favoured contractors.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Capitalist and conservative; the abolition of wages is alien to the movement.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Erdogan wants central bank policy under his control but not abolition of the bank.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: There is no state-recognised wage-and-price bargaining system; the nearest analogue is patronage links with business associations.

one-party-rule.rationale: The AKP rules through competitive elections under a dominant-party system rather than doctrine of a single legitimate party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Erdogan evokes Ottoman glory but operates a republic and presidency, not monarchy.

democracy-best.rationale: The movement claims democratic legitimacy through the national will, though critics note it weakens liberal checks.

direct-votes.rationale: Referendums are used for constitutional change in 2010 and 2017, but not as a general doctrine.

right-to-secede.rationale: The movement defends national unity and opposes regional secession, especially Kurdish.

natural-rulers.rationale: Charismatic leadership is celebrated but not framed as natural rule by a class.

political-violence-never.rationale: Erdogan portrays Turkey's military operations and counter-terror as justified, but condemns political violence by opponents.

war-builds-character.rationale: Martial national pride and sacrifice narratives appear, but peace and development are the official frame.

separate-church-state.rationale: The project explicitly moves beyond strict Kemalist secularism and uses Diyanet as a state instrument.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Turkey's legal code remains secular and the AKP denies seeking sharia, though policy is guided by Islamic morals.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The movement supports a strong state security and judicial apparatus.

military-superiority.rationale: Defence industry growth and regional power projection are signature themes.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Erdogan-ism defines the nation by Sunni Muslim identity more than ethnicity, though Turkish nationalism has grown within it.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Conservative-nationalist movement rejects class conflict as the driver of history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: It supports aid to the poor but not equality of outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not a theme, and Kurdish autonomy claims are resisted.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Erdogan rhetoric attacks Western colonialism, but reparations are not a stated policy.

civilizational-union.rationale: Erdogan presents Turkey as leader of the ummah and calls for Muslim unity under Turkish leadership.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Conservative-Islamic morality stresses family and community duty over self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Emphasis on family, community and national duty over individual autonomy is central to the rhetoric.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: No notable stance; environmentalism is secondary to development.

limit-population.rationale: Erdogan urges at least three children and calls the falling birthrate a crisis.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The movement is pro-industrial, mega-project oriented.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Technology self-reliance is celebrated, while disruption of established institutions is not an aim.

human-enhancement.rationale: Moral conservatism implies suspicion of transhumanist projects, though it is not addressed.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Personalist leadership does not fit delegation to algorithms.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: The state has restricted online platforms and expanded surveillance, so unbreakable encryption would conflict with its security approach.

restore-past-order.rationale: Ottoman-Islamic revival is a theme, yet the movement also stresses progress and development.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Erdogan's rhetoric stresses delivery, services and growth, though he strongly asserts ideological convictions.

direct-action.rationale: The movement relies on elections and state power, and condemns street protests such as Gezi.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The movement supports charity and aid but also private profit and market distribution.

production-for-use.rationale: A market economy with state support for business.

collective-farming.rationale: Not part of the movement; it favours private ownership.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Erdogan blames Western powers for conflict, but not capitalism as such.

taxation-theft.rationale: The state is large and taxes are accepted as the funding of national projects.

harm-principle.rationale: The movement endorses moral regulation of private conduct, for example on LGBT and family issues.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Emphasis on family, community and ummah over individualism.

conscription.rationale: Turkey maintains conscription and the AKP has not abolished it, only shortening service and adding paid exemptions.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The movement relies on electoral legitimacy and national loyalty.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is portrayed as the guardian of the nation, not as a firm.

positive-liberty.rationale: Social programmes are valued, but the concept is not articulated.

media-academia-power.rationale: Erdogan's populism targets media, academia and secular elites as hostile and powerful.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The movement defines identity through religion and history, not racial genetics.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation is through party and elections, not guild or family bodies.

total-state.rationale: The state is strong and expanding but the movement is not totalitarian in doctrine.

national-rebirth.rationale: The "New Turkey" and the 2023 vision are explicit programmes of national rebirth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Regional influence-seeking and military operations in Syria and Iraq reflect a maximalist foreign policy.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The leadership is personalised but not feudal.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Religious-conservative movement upholds truths based on faith and tradition, not power-relativism.

universal-morality.rationale: Islamic moral truths are asserted as universal, though adherents ground them in revelation more than reason.

single-common-good.rationale: The "national will" framing holds that a single people has one will.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Erdogan strongly criticises Israel, though trade and relations were maintained.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: No notable stance; Turkey grants easier citizenship to some diaspora groups.

revive-national-language.rationale: Turkish is in everyday use; the question is moot.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Not part of its pro-business stance.

school-vouchers.rationale: The AKP expanded public religious schools but not a voucher scheme.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Erdogan pursued growth-first policy, though he says he keeps fiscal discipline.

economic-freedom.rationale: Not a stated principle of the later movement.

rule-by-example.rationale: Piety and exemplary leaders are valued, but law and coercion are used heavily.

national-self-determination.rationale: Erdogan champions self-determination in rhetoric against Western tutelage, but resists it for Kurds.

force-without-un.rationale: Turkey has intervened in Syria, Iraq and Libya without UN authorisation.

reason-over-faith.rationale: A religious-conservative movement ranks faith and tradition above secular rationalism.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Turkey gives refugees limited services; no clear programme to limit welfare.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The movement has not taken a stated position on work requirements; its social assistance is largely unconditional or family-based.

class-collaboration.rationale: The movement calls for social harmony, business and worker cooperation, and opposes class politics.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The movement prizes the preservation of Ottoman-Islamic heritage.

dominated-front.rationale: Erdogan frames the "new world order" as unfair and invites cooperation among non-Western states.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Erdogan describes distinct roles of women as mothers and has rejected equal treatment of men and women.

ban-interest.rationale: Erdogan calls interest the mother of all evils and cites Islamic prohibition, but no legal ban has been enacted.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Rejected by a movement that stresses Muslim brotherhood.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy independence and domestic energy extraction are priorities, including Black Sea gas.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Syrian refugees are treated as guests, with mixed integration goals.

elite-replacement.rationale: No documented use of the Great Replacement idea as a core claim.

proportional-representation.rationale: Turkey already uses party-list PR with a threshold; the AKP has benefitted from the threshold.

national-mission.rationale: Turkey is cast as leader of the Muslim world and legitimate Ottoman successor.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The movement rejects the feminist claim that society systematically favours men.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Anti-elite populism is core, with secular Kemalist and Gulenist elites cast as corrupt.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Inferred from the movement's pronatalist family policy; the Family Council source says nothing on eugenics.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The movement defends the security forces and resists scrutiny, though it prosecuted past coup-era abuses.

night-watchman-state.rationale: It supports a large state role.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Rejected by a movement stressing Muslim unity.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Formally affirmed, but sectarian and political divides narrow it in practice.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: No documented position on the general category.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Turkey has a uniform civil code since 1926 and the AKP has not changed that.

restrict-conversion.rationale: No documented movement; Turkey has no law restricting conversion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Rejected by a movement that celebrates Eid sacrifice.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The AKP expanded religious instruction and imam-hatip schools.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Legitimacy through electoral will is central to the movement's claims.

trade-surplus.rationale: Export-led growth is a government goal.

population-transfer.rationale: The party has resettled refugees but denies a policy of expelling minorities.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The state defends its military operations abroad.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The government pursued bans or closure cases against Kurdish parties and the opposition, justifying them by security.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The movement favours concentrated executive power, which conflicts with the idea.

separated-powers.rationale: The 2017 presidential system concentrated power in the presidency and weakened checks on it, while keeping formally separate courts and parliament.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The AKP's appeal included social assistance to poor conservative constituencies.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: The housing agency TOKI sells homes, but council tenant rights are not a theme.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Governments under Erdogan have postponed strikes by decree on national-security grounds, and ballot requirements are in Turkish labour law.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Erdogan treats population growth as strength and a falling birthrate as the problem, so he rejects blaming people for poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Cohesion is framed through shared Sunni Muslim identity rather than ethnic homogeneity, so adherents are split.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Alien to a leader-centred electoral movement.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: After the 2016 coup attempt the government ruled by emergency decree for two years against its declared internal enemies.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Erdogan's government has used price pressure and inspections on food during inflation spikes and blames speculators.

party-controls-media.rationale: Government-aligned ownership dominates the media, but the movement does not endorse formal party control as doctrine.

party-commands-army.rationale: The military was brought under civilian control and the president now commands it, rather than the party as such.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: No documented position; Turkish citizenship rules have been loosened for investors.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not a stated position of the movement.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The AKP is a highly disciplined, leader-driven party.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Turkey sought EU membership early on, but later rhetoric is soft Eurosceptic and stresses sovereignty.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The 2017 presidential system gives the president command of the forces and power to appoint ministers.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not applicable to Sunni Islam; the equivalent state-run Diyanet is hierarchical.

clerical-rule.rationale: The movement denies seeking theocracy and keeps political authority with the elected leader.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Erdogan-aligned authorities have restricted art, broadcasts and media on moral grounds.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Erdogan has been in office since 2003, and the system supports his repeated candidacies.

recall-officials.rationale: Not a stance of the movement, which concentrates power.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Turkey remains in NATO, though the leadership criticises Western allies.

people-in-arms.rationale: The state strengthens a professional army and defence industry.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The base is provincial and pious, but the movement is urbanising and construction-driven.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Turkey supports the Turkish Cypriot state, but reunification of nations is not a general principle.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Populist rhetoric depicts secular, educated elites as out of touch with the people.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Civilizational-populist rhetoric ranks Islamic civilization against a corrupt West.

death-penalty.rationale: Erdogan said he would approve restoration of the death penalty after the 2016 coup attempt.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Erdogan attacks "desexualization" and gender-equality framing is resisted, though schools do give some health education.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The government curtailed evolution in the school curriculum in 2017.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Socially conservative government blocks pornography sites under Turkish law.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Turkey uses descent-based citizenship, but the party has not argued for it.

minority-language-support.rationale: The AKP expanded Kurdish-language rights in the early 2010s, but later reversed course.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The AKP lifted the headscarf ban, which was an exemption for pious Muslims, yet Alevi demands were largely refused.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: A conservative movement is opposed to eccentric ways of living.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Erdogan criticises Western financial power, but Turkey repays its debts.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Economic independence from the West is a theme, but not property transformation.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Erdogan's constitution-drafting drew on the AKP majority and referendum rather than a constituent assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The movement trades liberties for stability and growth in practice, though it does not endorse the idea as doctrine.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Turkey presents itself as one of the world's largest aid donors relative to income.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Erdogan has complained Turkey cannot have nuclear weapons while others do.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Erdogan introduced direct presidential election in 2014 and the presidential system in 2017.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Erdogan insisted on lowering rates and replaced central bank governors.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Turkey keeps northern Cyprus and does not trade Cyprus territory; the party held the Kurdish peace process on other grounds.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Islamic and conservative property ethics hold this, though the movement protects property in practice.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Not part of the movement's debates.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Growth and mega-project priorities override precaution.

collective-defense.rationale: Turkey stays in NATO and invokes Article 5 commitments.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Turkey does not recognise the annexation of Crimea.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Diyanet is a state body staffed by the party, though the movement itself wants more religion, not less.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Erdogan is a partisan president who remains the AKP's leader.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Turkey has fought the PKK for decades and rejects Kurdish secession.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The AKP resists regional autonomy even for Kurds.

sacred-ruler.rationale: A cult of personality exists, but not divine descent.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Turkey has progressive income tax and the AKP has not proposed a flat tax.

character-from-environment.rationale: The movement stresses upbringing in the family and also innate nature.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Critics say Erdogan is above the law, but he claims to be bound by it and the national will.

space-expansion.rationale: A Turkish space programme has been announced as a national-prestige project.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The ideology favours executive power backed by popular majority rather than mixed rule.

leader-cult.rationale: Erdogan-ism relies on a cult of personality and is described by scholars as based on charismatic authority.

equal-parenting.rationale: No documented stance, though family-first ideology emphasises mothers.

land-redistribution.rationale: Rejected by a pro-property conservative movement.

refugee-return.rationale: Turkey champions Palestinian rights and supports return of Syrian refugees to Syria.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Turkey invokes protection of Turkic and Muslim kin communities but has made no formal claim.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The party denies seeking sharia, and apostasy is not a crime in Turkey, though social conservatism is hostile.

women-must-cover.rationale: The AKP campaigned for the right to wear a headscarf, not for a legal requirement.

common-currency.rationale: Turkey keeps the lira and treats currency sovereignty as an element of independence.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-Turkic and Ottoman-Islamic cooperation themes exist through the Organization of Turkic States.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The AKP resists minority self-governing schools and institutions.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: A Marxist claim rejected by the movement.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition law exists, but state-favoured business groups dominate.

no-bailouts.rationale: The government has regularly supported banks and firms with credit guarantees.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The ideology puts the national will above checks and balances and critics call it an elective dictatorship.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The movement rejects gender quotas in favour of women's family roles.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Turkey seeks export and investment integration, though it values domestic production.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: A low-wage export economy is wary of binding standards.

moral-incentives.rationale: Religious duty is invoked, but market incentives remain.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The movement fights the PKK and condemns armed insurgents.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Turkey has no titles, and the republic abolished them; Erdogan does not defend hereditary privilege despite Ottoman nostalgia.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The AKP revised school history to centre Ottoman-Islamic heritage.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Erdogan attacks Western tutelage, though his Ottoman nostalgia casts Turkey as leader of Muslims.

patriotic-education.rationale: Nationalist, religious and patriotic education is central to its schools policy.

public-money-creation.rationale: Erdogan wants cheap state-influenced credit, but no public money creation scheme.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: A pro-capitalist movement expects markets to adapt.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Neo-Ottomanism is a foreign policy based on influence in former Ottoman lands.

delink-world-market.rationale: Turkey seeks integration into trade and finance.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist thesis foreign to the movement.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Not a movement concern, but it opposes a libertarian absolute.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The party promises rights in its programme, but the ideology gives less weight to checks.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Erdogan challenges the Treaty of Lausanne and Sevres narratives rhetorically, but no formal repudiation.

elective-rulers.rationale: The movement's claim to legitimacy is electoral.

minority-veto.rationale: Majoritarian national will contradicts minority vetoes.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: A leader-centred movement rejects resistance to its ruler.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The 2017 system shifted power from parliament to the president.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: The government passed a controversial 2021 stray-animal law, but Islamic tradition recognises kindness to animals.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Islamic practice allows animal use with humane requirements.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Charity and aid to the poor are encouraged by Islamic-conservative ethics.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The movement holds that mass culture can corrupt, but not the critical-theory claim.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian claim not used by the movement.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Erdogan blames Western economic power for Turkey's currency crisis but does not adopt dependency theory.

native-born-offices.rationale: Turkish law requires citizenship for public posts, with no stated native-born rule.

party-own-road.rationale: A communist-movement question with no application to a conservative-nationalist party, so no position is documented.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The leadership stresses economic independence and rejects IMF conditionality, while accepting foreign investment.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Erdogan has hinted at Ottoman-era claims but no formal demand.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anti-fascism is not a stated founding value of the AKP.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not an issue for the movement.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: The AKP replaced Kemalist symbols and is thus inconsistent.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Turkey left the Istanbul Convention in 2021, but not through symmetry claims.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The ideology holds that Turkey needs its own model, as Orban's "illiberal democracy" is said to parallel.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The AKP brought the military under civilian control and ended the Kemalist guardianship.

paid-care-work.rationale: Family policy stresses motherhood, but no stated position on paying care work.

filial-duty.rationale: Erdogan stresses family morality, and respect for elders is central to Islamic-conservative ethics.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil service exams exist, but critics find patronage in appointments.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Turkey courts foreign investment while keeping strategic sectors such as defence under state or allied control, so adherents are not clearly committed either way.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Erdogan laments rising divorce rates and the party has considered measures to discourage it.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The AKP introduced private pension supplements but kept the state system.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliament still approves the budget but the 2017 system gave the president strong budget powers.

single-official-language.rationale: Turkish is the sole official language and the AKP has not shifted that despite earlier Kurdish gestures.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Turkey has liberalised foreign property purchases, a significant source of investment.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Not an issue for the movement, and rejected.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Turkey backed Syrian opposition factions and Muslim Brotherhood offshoots.

corporate-influence.rationale: Cronyism is a critique of the AKP itself, but is not an adherent view.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The government accuses foreign-funded NGOs and media of working against the state.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Erdogan urges three children and has declared 2026-2035 the decade of family and population.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The movement stresses obedience to the national will.

non-intervention.rationale: Turkey has intervened in neighbours' affairs while demanding others not intervene in its own.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Erdogan's rhetoric accuses Gulenists and foreign-backed groups and blames an "interest-rate lobby" and foreign powers for economic troubles.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Rejected by a movement that holds marriage sacred.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Turkey has a freedom-of-information law, but the party restricts media and transparency.

local-production.rationale: Domestic production is encouraged, but not as a principle.

informal-organisation.rationale: The movement is a hierarchical party.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Erdogan's government has declined to follow ECHR rulings, and treats national courts as supreme.

religious-nation.rationale: The "Muslim-Turkish nation" framing defines the national community by religion as much as ethnicity.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Its neo-Ottoman, civilizational-populist foreign policy asserts Turkey as a leader and rejects Western tutelage, so submission to another power is inferred as rejected.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred: Erdoğanism favours a centralised presidency and national unity framing, so regions keeping their revenue is inferred as rejected.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Inferred from its pro-business, pro-property conservative economics.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred from its conservative-nationalist roots, which have been historically hostile to communism; not a stated focus.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The AKP's health transformation expanded coverage while using private hospitals and public-private partnerships, so mixed provision is inferred as accepted.

religion-illusion.rationale: The ideology fuses conservative Islam with the national identity, treating religion as a lasting source of values rather than an illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The AKP is pro-growth and pro-business, building its record on construction, investment and market-driven expansion.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from its pious-family agenda and view of women's role centred on motherhood and family, not economic transformation.

socialized-care.rationale: The family-centred agenda treats childcare and household work as the family's role, with pronatalist incentives rather than public provision.

purge-loanwords.rationale: The ideology is anti-Kemalist, and the Turkish Language Association's purism is a Kemalist legacy, so a loanword purge is inferred as rejected.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred: the state treats minorities within borders as bound by national unity; treaty-based claims are not recognised as a constraint.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred: self-governing communal property conflicts with its centralised, pro-business conservatism.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred: it stresses national unity and Islamic brotherhood across ethnic lines rather than majority settlement of minority regions.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Inferred: it is a market-friendly conservative programme that does not present itself as a third way between capitalism and communism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred from the neo-Ottoman strand of Erdoğanism, which treats former Ottoman lands and peoples as a sphere of Turkish historical responsibility.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Inferred: nothing in the sources endorses denial; Erdoğan attacks Israel but on Gaza and Palestine, not by denying the Holocaust.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Homosexuality is not a crime in Turkey under the AKP, but Erdoğan presents LGBT identities as a threat to the sacred family, so adherents oppose recognition rather than demand prosecution.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Yilmaz and Morieson document repression of opponents, media and civil society, justified as defending the national will against elite and foreign plots.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred from the Diyanet-backed defence of Islamic values and insult-to-religion prosecutions under the AKP; no source states a doctrine on punishing blasphemy.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred: the programme is nationalist and Ottoman-nostalgic, but frames Turkey as anti-imperialist rather than endorsing colonial rule for profit.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred: Erdoğanism backs Muslim causes rhetorically but acts through state diplomacy and military power, not a personal duty of every Muslim.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred: Erdoğanism claims power through elections and the national will, and presents itself as the victim of coups, not as a movement for removing rulers by force.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The presidential system and cult of personality concentrate decisions in one leader rather than in local or workplace participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred from the civilizational-populist framing, which stresses a unified pious nation and rejects identity-based critiques of its social order.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Erdoğan has denounced LGBT identities as a threat to the family and has spoken of desexualization, so legal recognition is opposed.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred from the pious-family agenda and religious conservatism, which treat life as sacred; not directly addressed in the sources.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Inferred: Erdoğanism defines itself against secular elites and claims a distinct conservative-Islamic side, not a synthesis of left and right.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred: the programme is pro-growth and pro-capital, with no critique of wage labour as alienating.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Erdoğanism holds that Islam is part of Turkey's Ottoman-Islamic self, set against a West it sees as hostile, so it rejects the claim that Islam is incompatible with Western values.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Erdoğanism grounds legitimacy in the national will expressed through elections, though its Islamist component gives religion a large public role.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The AKP lifted the headscarf ban for civil servants and students, so it rejects banning religious dress in state institutions.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; a pro-business conservative government and a pro-women rhetoric pull in opposite directions.

social-market-economy.rationale: The AKP record combines privatisation and market growth with expanded state health coverage and social assistance.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Assertive, militarised foreign policy and neo-Ottoman ambitions make the armed forces central to Erdoğanism.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from Erdoğan's pro-growth, construction-led economy that favours business growth; not stated as a doctrine.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Turkey stays in NATO but Erdoğan pursues multi-alignment, buying Russian arms and balancing blocs, so he rejects exclusive membership of one but also does not choose neutrality.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Erdoğanism rests on a republican claim to the national will, not hereditary rule, though family ties at the top are noted; inferred.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Erdoğan attacks interest and backs Islamic participation finance, but his model is state-steered growth rather than user-owned mutual banks; inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Erdoğan's rhetoric casts IMF conditionality as foreign tutelage and he stresses economic sovereignty; inferred.

property-franchise.rationale: A populist claim to embody the whole national will is incompatible with wealth-based franchise limits; inferred.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The pious-family agenda and rejection of feminism make a link between ending domination of women and nature unlikely; inferred.

reification.rationale: A Marxist critique of capitalist alienation is foreign to a conservative, pro-growth Islamic nationalism; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Adherents deny that wealth controls the press, and allied business interests own much of the media; inferred from the pro-business, anti-leftist stance.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The 2017 presidential system concentrates decree power in one person, and adherents defend strong personal rule over checks; inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: Citizenship is defined as Turkish and inclusive in form, so an ethnic franchise is not an Erdoğanist position; inferred.

online-participation.rationale: The party uses social media heavily for mobilisation but controls and restricts online discourse; adherents are split; inferred.

open-government-data.rationale: A centralised, personalised executive favours discretion over open records; inferred.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: A socially conservative, Islam-inflected movement is inclined to favour religious endogamy norms; inferred at low confidence.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Adherents claim to protect minorities' standing and economic nationalism is aimed at foreign, not minority, firms; inferred.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Plebiscitary populism prefers elections and the leader's mandate to deliberative panels; inferred.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: A conservative pious-family agenda favours received religious norms over reinterpretation, though state-run religious authority adapts doctrine; inferred.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Erdoğanism favours a pro-growth, business-friendly state and does not frame wealth concentration as a threat to liberty; inferred.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Erdoğan's family-centred agenda and rhetoric treat LGBT rights as a threat to the family and national values.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The ideology is Islam-inflected and aims to raise a pious generation, so it opposes state promotion of atheism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Erdoğanism favours a strong, centralised state and security apparatus, and abolitionism is far from its positions.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The movement stresses a unitary national will and a strong presidency over sharing executive power between communities; inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The AKP combines religious charity networks with an expanded state welfare system, so adherents do not take either side; inferred.

term-limits.rationale: Erdoğan has served as party leader, prime minister and president since 2003, and the 2017 system strengthened the presidency; limits sit badly with it.

vote-delegation.rationale: The ideology favours a personalised, centralised presidency and electoral majorities, not delegable votes; inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Nothing in the programme prioritises extinction risk; its priorities are growth, family and national strength; inferred.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Socially conservative Islamic thought generally keeps religious leadership male; inferred, with the family agenda as context.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Erdoğan has said women and men are not equal and promotes a family model with traditional roles; inferred from the family agenda.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Nationalist-populist 'national will' politics ties the vote to citizens; inferred.

rent-control.rationale: A pro-growth, construction-led economy leans against caps, but Erdogan's government has accepted limits, so adherents are split; inferred.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed; a pro-business, nationalist programme leans against abolition, inferred.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The pious-youth and national-identity agenda favours organising young people around national and religious values; inferred.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Turkey hosts NATO nuclear weapons and Erdogan has said Turkey should not be denied nuclear weapons; inferred.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Turkey remains in NATO and hosts allied bases at Incirlik; sovereignty rhetoric exists, but an anti-base line is not part of the ideology.

recognise-genocide.rationale: The government rejects calling the Armenian killings genocide; inferred from its civilizational-populist nationalism.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Erdogan calls interest the mother of all evil, treating unearned income as wrong; inferred for this broader claim.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Not addressed; a nationalist, martial-minded movement rejects the claim, inferred.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Neo-Ottomanist and nationalist narratives stress long historical continuity; inferred.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Erdogan calls LGBT identities an attack on the family and treats sex roles as fixed.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: A pious-family agenda that treats women as mothers conflicts with this claim; inferred.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Honouring the 'sehit' (martyr) is central to the nationalist-Islamic politics; inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Civilizational populism frames politics as a struggle between a pious people and elites; inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Neo-Ottoman and civilizational politics treat Turkey as a leading centre for Turks and Muslims abroad; inferred.

culture-before-state.rationale: The programme pursues state power and a strong presidency alongside cultural conservatism; inferred.

god-not-male.rationale: An Islam-inflected conservative movement keeps traditional language for God; inferred.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: A pious-family conservative programme rejects this approach to scripture; inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: A 'national and native' economic agenda and pious business class are favoured; inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Centralised leadership and a unitary-state nationalism oppose ethnic regional units; inferred.

independent-unions.rationale: The strong-presidency, state-aligned style distrusts autonomous institutions; inferred.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Erdoğanism is populist and nationalist, not socialist, and claims to embody the national will; inferred.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The state-steered economy includes both public services and privatization; adherents are split.

second-chamber.rationale: Turkey is unicameral and the programme favours a concentrated presidency over extra checks; inferred.

municipal-property.rationale: A pro-growth, state-steered but private-enterprise economy; community ownership of production is alien to it.

confederal-coordination.rationale: A centralised unitary state with a personalised presidency leaves no room for governing-free confederations.

family-wage.rationale: The pious-family agenda supports family-centred policy, as in the Family Council in s4.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: A pro-growth, state-building programme favours faster health-sector development; inferred.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed; no principle bears clearly on it.

anonymous-payments.rationale: A centralised state seeking control over finance is unlikely to back untraceable payments; inferred.

online-anonymity.rationale: The strong-state, anti-opposition style disfavours anonymity online; inferred.

person-over-state.rationale: The populist claim to embody the national will places the collective above individual claims; inferred.

spiritual-nature.rationale: An Islam-inflected, pious-family programme treats politics as serving religious as well as material life.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: A centralised unitary state leaves regional powers dependent on the national legislature; inferred.

gm-crops.rationale: Conservative nationalist and Islam-inflected opinion in Turkey has been wary of GM crops; inferred.

dense-cities.rationale: The programme favours construction-led growth but is not framed by environmental claims; adherents are split.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Turkish nationalism and civilizational populism are national and religious, not racial; inferred.

racial-pride.rationale: Pride in nation and Ottoman heritage is central, but framed as civilizational, not racial; adherents are split.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The assertive Ottoman-influenced foreign policy involves interventions abroad, as s2 describes.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Erdoğanism anchors the nation in Turkish-Islamic identity and the national will, not language alone, and it is wary of language-based ethnic claims; inferred from that civilizational framing.

communal-electorates.rationale: Its majoritarian national-will claim and unitary-state nationalism run against separate religious electorates; inferred, as the programme never addresses the question.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Erdoğanist rhetoric regularly casts foreign powers and domestic proxies as plotting to divide and weaken Turkey, in the Sèvres-syndrome tradition.

free-public-college.rationale: Turkish state universities already charge little or no tuition and AKP governments expanded places; inferred as a mild yes, not a stated principle.

pollution-taxes.rationale: The pro-growth, construction-led economic model gives priority to output over environmental levies; inferred from that emphasis.

future-generations.rationale: Conservative and religious stewardship of the family and nation implies obligation to future generations; inferred, not a stated plank.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Erdoğan stresses women's distinct role as mothers and rejects gender equality as such, but does not argue for weighting women's values in public life; adherents are split on the reading.

arms-reduction.rationale: The programme builds up a national defence industry and assertive military power, so cutting arms to the minimum is not a priority; inferred.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Diplomacy is highly personalised around the president and conducted through leader-level deals; inferred that open diplomacy is not a principle.

capital-controls.rationale: The state-steered but investment-seeking growth model relies on foreign capital inflows, though Erdoğan attacks 'interest lobbies'; net inferred against controls.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: A strong centralised state with a monopoly on force is central, justified against terrorism and the Gulenist network.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Civilizational populism treats national defence and the army's service to the nation as sacred.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Pro-business, state-steered growth with government-friendly unions; inferred from the economic record.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Social transfers are used but in-work credits specifically are not a documented position.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Erdogan favours state-led growth and low interest rates, but the AKP also has a record of budget discipline; adherents are split.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Civilizational populism criticises the Western-dominated order, as in the slogan that the world is bigger than five.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Erdoganism took over and expanded the state under presidential control rather than dismantling it.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred from a centralised, state-steered economy with a fixed national developmental project.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred from a construction- and growth-led development model that subordinates ecology to growth.

sacred-nation.rationale: The nation and its historic community are central, and the leader is claimed to embody the national will.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred from the centralised nationalism and the rejection of Kurdish regional grievances.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from its conservative family agenda, which treats the traditional family and sexes as natural and opposes gender redefinition.

public-service-media.rationale: Broadcasting and the press are widely documented as under government influence, and critics of the media are attacked.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Inferred from the Sunni-Ottoman Islamic framing of the national self, which does not treat all religions as equivalent.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from the AKP's state-steered, pro-rural economic approach; farm support is not a defining issue.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from the assertive, sovereignty-focused foreign policy and Erdogan's complaints that nuclear powers deny others such weapons.

workers-own-party.rationale: The ideology claims to speak for the whole nation through one leader and party, so a separate class party is inferred as unwelcome.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not an Erdogan theme; the conservative pious-family agenda and existing Turkish law point toward prohibition.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Turkish civil law already gives equal rights and the AKP has not contested them; inferred as mild support.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed; Turkish-nationalist and Kurdish-sensitive positions leave adherents split on how regional languages are named.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from its state-steered, growth-first economy, which favours agency and executive control over private tort remedies.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: The ideology centralizes power in the presidency, so a formal chiefs' advisory role is inferred as unwelcome.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Erdogan's growth-first, construction-heavy economic approach puts development ahead of environmental limits.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from its law-and-order, strong-state outlook.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from its national-unity and Turkish-identity stress; language requirements for newcomers fit its nationalism.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: The AKP's record on unions is mixed and Erdogan has not made compulsory membership an issue, so this is inferred as neutral.

voter-id.rationale: A nationalist, order-minded programme favours identity checks at the polls, but Erdogan has not made it a campaign position, so this is inferred.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: State religious affairs under the AKP privilege the Sunni Hanafi mainstream, and the pious-conservative programme does not equalize interpretations such as Alevism.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Erdogan's populism rests on a claim to embody the national will won at the ballot box, so electoral victory is the core of democratic legitimacy for adherents.

premarital-sex.rationale: The pious-family agenda promotes marriage and chastity and Erdogan has said women should be mothers first, so adherents would not accept sex outside marriage.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Turkish authorities under the AKP have throttled access after unrest and attacks; adherents justify it as protecting order, but this is inferred from practice.

negative-income-tax.rationale: The state-steered, patronage-based welfare model favours in-kind and discretionary support over a negative income tax, so mild disagreement is inferred.

women-suffrage.rationale: Women vote and hold office under the AKP and it counts the 2007 and later increases in female deputies among its record, so equal political rights are accepted.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Erdogan holds that Islam gives women honour and that the harm lies in secular modernity, so adherents reject religion as a cause of oppression.

race-social-construct.rationale: The programme gives no stated view on racial categories; its civilizational populism stresses culture and religion over race.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Erdogan rejects equality of men and women in favour of 'equity' and Turkey left the Istanbul Convention, so adherents back family-centred bodies rather than equality agencies.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the state-steered, state-centred economy in s3; unowned land is treated as public property, not claimable by first use.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred: Erdoğan calls for trials of foreign leaders such as Israel's but rejects outside scrutiny of Turkey, so adherents are split.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Inferred from the Islam-inflected conservatism in s1; the programme is pious but does not state a doctrine on literal reading.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the sacred-family agenda in s4, which stresses traditional roles over gender-equality guarantees.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred from the pro-growth, privatising record in s3, which is hostile to nationalised planned economies.

indirect-election.rationale: The populist claim to embody the national will rests on direct popular election, as in the 2017 presidential system.

national-church-status.rationale: The state-run Diyanet gives Sunni Islam a privileged public status that Erdoğan's governments have expanded.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Nationalist centralisation under the presidential system opposes territorial autonomy for Kurdish-majority regions.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred: Erdoğan backs self-determination for Turkish Cypriots but rejects votes such as Crimea's, so adherents' stance is selective.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred from the neo-Ottoman strand, which questions the post-Ottoman borders drawn after the First World War.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from the growth-first agenda in s5, which favours expanding consumption and construction over limited needs.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist, centralising stance in s1, which does not favour regional protections against settlers.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred: Turkey keeps male-only conscription and the sacred-family agenda in s4 assigns women a different role.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred from Erdoğan's nationalist and Ottoman-influenced rhetoric about the homeland; not stated directly in the sources.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred: Erdoğanism stresses a strong state but frames it through law and courts; the sources do not discuss killing drug suspects.

close-ties-china.rationale: Inferred from an assertive, multi-aligned foreign policy that is not tied mainly to the US; contested.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Its civilizational-populist foreign policy claims a duty toward Turks and kin communities abroad.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred: a nationalist, pro-growth, state-steered economy is not framed around global common ownership of resources.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred from its pious-family agenda and communitarian conservatism, which put family and community above individual autonomy.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: The sources do not address consumption taxes, and Erdoğan's policy has varied.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: The sources do not settle this; the AKP has used both targeted aid and broad programmes.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The sources describe a populist claim to embody the national will directly, with a personalised presidency over intermediaries.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from documented AKP-linked patronage and state-steered business; adherents would likely not accept the premise.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Erdoğanism is Islam-inflected and rejects the secular elite's exclusion of religion from politics.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Erdoğanism pairs economic and technological growth with a pious, tradition-based family and cultural agenda.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Adherents are split: the pious-family agenda is conservative, yet Turkish civil law already grants this right.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred from nationalist, state-steered economic policy and sovereignty rhetoric; not documented in detail.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Erdoganism tolerates inequality through business growth and patronage but does not state a process-based theory of just distribution, so it is inferred as split.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Erdogan favours a pro-growth, business-friendly economy and a sovereigntist stance, so a new international tax is inferred to be unwelcome.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Turkish debate on racism is framed differently, and the strand's stance on this American-framed claim is inferred rather than documented.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Erdoganism puts the national will and state authority above judicial objection, so a right to resist unjust law is inferred to be rejected.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Erdogan stresses growth, jobs and a pious family agenda; automation to cut work is not discussed, so it is inferred as neutral.

multipolar-world.rationale: The civilizational-populist foreign policy casts the West as a rival to an Ottoman-Islamic self and seeks an assertive independent role, which fits several centres of power.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Erdoganism is conservative, Islamic and pro-market and has no Marxist economic theory; the labour theory of value is rejected.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Erdogan's populism claims to serve ordinary Turks and love of nation, but it is inferred rather than stated as a union of patriotism and labour politics.

material-over-identity.rationale: Erdoganism stresses cultural and religious identity but also courts ordinary working people with material benefits, and it is not framed in left-right strategy terms, so it is split.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Erdoganism is a pro-market conservative-Islamic nationalism, and a communist-party-led system is the opposite of its political project.

missingStatements.text: Interest rates are a cause of inflation, and governments should push them down to fight it.
missingStatements.rationale: Erdoğan repeatedly says interest rates are the mother of all evils and the cause of inflation.

missingStatements.text: Women should be encouraged to have at least three children.
missingStatements.rationale: Erdoğan says 'we do not say have at least three children for nothing' and treats population growth as national strength.

missingStatements.text: The national will expressed at the ballot box should outweigh the objections of courts, the press and other institutions.
missingStatements.rationale: The ideology puts electoral consent above separation of powers; critics call the result an elective dictatorship.

notes: The early AKP (2002-2010) was more liberal: pro-EU, pro-market and democratising, and many answers on checks and balances, Kurds and the EU would differ for that strand. Whether Erdoğanism is 'Islamist' is debated; the party itself says conservative democrat.
